reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general thermodynamic stabilization and synthesis of HEA nanoparticles but provides no specific data or findings on surface segregation, its effect on cohesive energy, or its influence on melting behavior. The key premises about surface heterogeneity and melting are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Surface chemical heterogeneity (segregation/short-range order) can be induced in HEA nanoparticles by moderate annealing
Surface heterogeneity reduces local cohesive energy at the nanoparticle surface
Reduced local cohesive energy lowers the onset temperature for premelting and melting
This effect is most pronounced in the 10–50 nm size regime where surface energy dominates
As-synthesized HEA nanoparticles are uniformly mixed with minimal surface segregation
